note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set.

checkers.alarm: (A.dag().dag() - A).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*max(1, A.norm('max'))
checkers.invariant: dag() is an involution: A.dag().dag() == A
checkers.observation_point: inside dag(), immediately before returning, re-calling dag() on the freshly computed result
checkers.precondition: any Qobj of type oper/super/ket/bra, any data layer (Dense/CSR/Dia), any dimension, Hermitian or not
checkers.rationale: dag() dispatches through a per-data-layer _data.adjoint path or an _isherm short-circuit; a divergence between the two after two applications would corrupt every inner product and Hermiticity check in the library
checkers.scientific_quantity: Hermitian adjoint of a quantum operator

checkers.alarm: purity < 1/d - tol or purity > 1 + tol, tol = 50*eps64*d + 3*d*atol_tidy
checkers.invariant: 1/d <= purity <= 1 for any valid density matrix of dimension d
checkers.observation_point: inside purity(), before returning, for operator-type inputs only
checkers.precondition: any Hermitian, positive-semidefinite, unit-trace operator-type Qobj of dimension d >= 1 (ket/bra branch excluded as a local tautology per SANITIZER.md 5.6)
checkers.rationale: purity is the standard mixedness diagnostic used throughout the solver stack; a value outside [1/d, 1] means the input was not a valid density matrix or the Tr(rho^2) computation is wrong
checkers.scientific_quantity: purity Tr(rho^2) of a quantum state

checkers.alarm: abs(result.unit(norm).norm(norm) - 1) exceeds 50*eps64
checkers.invariant: unit() is idempotent on its own fixed point: applying unit() to an already-unit-normalized object under the same norm returns an object whose norm is still 1
checkers.observation_point: inside unit(), before returning, when the input's own norm was already within tolerance of 1
checkers.precondition: any nonzero ket/bra/oper Qobj, any of the five supported norm choices, already normalized to within 1e-8 of unit norm before the re-call
checkers.rationale: unit() is the standard normalization entry point used by solver code; idempotence failure means repeated normalization does not converge to a fixed point, silently injecting systematic bias in iterative solvers
checkers.scientific_quantity: normalized representative of a quantum state or operator

checkers.alarm: either recovered factor differs from the expected Tr(other)*factor by more than 50*eps64*n*m*scale + 2*n*m*atol_tidy, scale = max(1, max|Tr(other)*factor|, max|factor|*sum_k|diag(other)_kk|)
checkers.invariant: tensor(A, B).ptrace([0]) == Tr(B)*A and tensor(A, B).ptrace([1]) == Tr(A)*B
checkers.observation_point: wired at tensor()'s own two-operand return site: immediately re-calls ptrace([0]) and ptrace([1]) on the freshly built product
checkers.precondition: any two square operator-type Qobjs A (dims [[n],[n]]) and B (dims [[m],[m]]), any data layer (CSR inputs in canonical format, no duplicate entries), Hermitian or not
checkers.rationale: ptrace and tensor are the two most basic composite-system primitives; a violation means the index bookkeeping in _data.ptrace and the Kronecker ordering in _data.kron are mutually inconsistent
checkers.scientific_quantity: partial trace as the adjoint of the tensor/embedding map

checkers.alarm: exact inequality (tol=0): permute is a pure relabeling with no floating-point arithmetic on the data itself, or an exception during the composed re-call
checkers.invariant: A.permute(sigma).permute(tau) == A.permute(composed), where composed[i] = sigma[tau[i]]
checkers.observation_point: inside permute(), stamping the applied order and originating object on the result; a second chained permute() call re-derives the composed order and re-calls permute() once more on the original object for comparison
checkers.precondition: any pure-dims bra/ket/square-oper Qobj with k >= 2 tensor factors, any two permutations sigma, tau of {0,...,k-1}, applied as two chained permute() calls; CSR inputs in canonical format (no duplicate entries)
checkers.rationale: permute is used to reconcile tensor-factor ordering across independently built composite systems; a broken composition law would silently scramble subsystem identity in exactly the multi-step permutation sequences real code uses
checkers.scientific_quantity: tensor-factor relabeling as a group action of the symmetric group

checkers.alarm: abs(overlap) exceeds 50*eps64 for distinct indices
checkers.invariant: basis(dims, n1).overlap(basis(dims, n2)) == 0 for n1 != n2, and == 1 for n1 == n2
checkers.observation_point: inside basis(), a re-call sanitizer constructs a second basis vector at a different valid index in the same space and checks the overlap
checkers.precondition: any flat (non-composite) dimension size >= 2, any integer basis index n, offset=0
checkers.rationale: every state built via fock_dm, thermal_dm, coherent, etc. assumes the basis is orthonormal; a broken dims2idx mapping colliding two distinct indices onto the same location would silently corrupt every downstream state
checkers.scientific_quantity: orthonormality of the Fock/computational basis of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space

checkers.alarm: abs(result.norm() - 1) exceeds 200*eps64*max(1,|alpha|) + sqrt(2N)*atol_tidy
checkers.invariant: coherent(N, alpha, method='operator').norm() == 1 for all valid inputs
checkers.observation_point: inside coherent(), before returning, in the method=='operator' branch
checkers.precondition: any N >= 1, any complex alpha, offset=0, method='operator' (the docstring's unconditional normalization guarantee is specific to this method, unlike 'analytic')
checkers.rationale: the docstring makes an explicit, unconditional normalization guarantee for the operator method (contrasted against analytic, which documents no such guarantee); downstream code that trusts this and skips its own .unit() call would silently accumulate error if the guarantee fails
checkers.scientific_quantity: coherent state D(alpha)|0> at finite truncation N

checkers.alarm: abs(pairwise overlap) exceeds 50*eps64 for any pair
checkers.invariant: the four Bell states are mutually orthonormal: all C(4,2)=6 pairwise overlaps are 0
checkers.observation_point: inside bell_state(), a re-call sanitizer constructs all four Bell states and checks all 6 pairwise overlaps
checkers.precondition: all four Bell states as constructed by the module's _BELL_STATES literal dict
checkers.rationale: a sign or index transcription error in exactly one of the four hard-coded literals would still yield a normalized state but break mutual orthogonality -- the actual scientifically meaningful property of a 'basis'
checkers.scientific_quantity: mutual orthonormality of the four hard-coded Bell states

checkers.alarm: (roundtrip - original).norm('max') exceeds 200*eps64*dim^4*scale
checkers.invariant: the Choi<->super transform pair is self-inverse: to_choi(to_super(to_choi(A))) == to_choi(A)
checkers.observation_point: inside to_choi/to_super, a re-call sanitizer applies the paired conversion twice and compares to the original
checkers.precondition: any super-type Qobj with superrep in {'super','choi'}, any valid pure dims including dimension-changing (non-square) maps, any data layer -- deliberately not restricted to CPTP maps, since the transform is a general basis reshuffle
checkers.rationale: to_choi/to_super are the two most heavily used representation converters; an involution failure means the reshape/transpose index arithmetic silently loses or misplaces information for some dimension family
checkers.scientific_quantity: equivalence of the Choi matrix and Liouville supermatrix representations of a linear map

checkers.alarm: worst observed action difference exceeds max(200*eps64*dim^2,2*dim^2*recall_tol)*scale; checker-side exceptions are not alarms
checkers.invariant: Sum_i K_i rho K_i^dag agrees, up to the explicit to_kraus truncation threshold, between the original Kraus list and to_kraus(kraus_to_choi(Ks)), for deterministic generic density matrices in the Kraus input space
checkers.observation_point: inside kraus_to_choi(), a re-call sanitizer round-trips through Choi and compares channel action on multiple test states
checkers.precondition: any list of Kraus operators (any count, consistent input/output dims, any data layer; CSR inputs in canonical format, no duplicate entries) -- automatically CP by construction
checkers.rationale: this is the central round trip a user relies on when moving between the Kraus-operator-list and single-Choi-matrix mental models of a channel
checkers.scientific_quantity: channel action equivalence of a Kraus decomposition round-tripped through the Choi representation

checkers.alarm: (roundtrip - original).norm('max') exceeds 400*eps64*dim^4*scale, or an exception during the round trip
checkers.invariant: to_choi(to_chi(J)) == J for J in Choi form, and to_super(to_choi(to_chi(to_super(S)))) == S for S in super form -- the full triangle closes in both directions
checkers.observation_point: inside to_chi(), a re-call sanitizer traverses the round trip and compares to the input
checkers.precondition: any qubit-dims (isqubitdims) super-type Qobj with superrep in {'super','choi','chi'} -- chi representation is qubit-only per the module's own isqubitdims gate
checkers.rationale: if any one of the three pairwise conversions has a subtle basis-ordering or normalization bug, the triangle fails to close even though each conversion individually looks like a valid matrix of the right shape
checkers.scientific_quantity: mutual consistency of the Choi, chi (Pauli-basis process matrix), and Liouville supermatrix representations of the same completely positive map

checkers.alarm: abs(fidelity(A,B) - fidelity(B,A)) exceeds 500*eps64 (+ 2x conditioning term, see tolerance_derivation)
checkers.invariant: fidelity(A, B) == fidelity(B, A)
checkers.observation_point: at every return point of fidelity(), a re-call sanitizer computes fidelity(B, A) and compares
checkers.precondition: any two Qobj of type ket/bra/oper with matching dimensions, operator case a valid density matrix, any relative scale or near-degeneracy Arguments of Qobj type 'super' (e.g. the Choi matrices qutip's process_fidelity passes to fidelity) are outside the precondition and are not checked (revised 2026-10-09).
checkers.rationale: the implementation is not symmetric in its code path (it branches on argument type and swaps for numerical stability when A is oper and B is ket/bra); a violation means the swap is not actually numerically neutral
checkers.scientific_quantity: Uhlmann fidelity between two density matrices

checkers.alarm: abs(fidelity(A,A) - 1) exceeds 2000*eps64 (+ 2x conditioning term, see tolerance_derivation)
checkers.invariant: fidelity(A, A) == 1
checkers.observation_point: at the operator-branch return point of fidelity(), when the two arguments are numerically identical (A.norm('max') diff to the other argument is exactly 0)
checkers.precondition: any single valid density matrix A, compared against itself, restricted to the operator branch (the ket/bra fast path is a local tautology and is excluded) Arguments of Qobj type 'super' (e.g. the Choi matrices qutip's process_fidelity passes to fidelity) are outside the precondition and are not checked (revised 2026-10-09).
checkers.rationale: a self-fidelity below 1 for a legitimately constructed density matrix would indicate numerical instability specifically in the mixed-state sqrtm/eigenenergies pipeline that the pure-state fast path never exercises
checkers.scientific_quantity: self-fidelity of a density matrix under the sqrtm+eigenvalue machinery

checkers.alarm: abs(tracedist(A,A)) exceeds 100*eps64, or abs(tracedist(A,B)-tracedist(B,A)) exceeds 100*eps64
checkers.invariant: tracedist(A,A) == 0 (self-distance), and tracedist(A,B) == tracedist(B,A) (symmetry)
checkers.observation_point: at the return point of tracedist(), a re-call sanitizer computes tracedist(A,A) and tracedist(B,A) and compares
checkers.precondition: any valid density matrices (or auto-projected ket/bra) A, B of matching dimensions
checkers.rationale: tracedist is documented and used as a genuine metric; if either axiom fails outside float noise, code that relies on it as a true metric (convergence criteria, optimization landscapes) would behave incorrectly
checkers.scientific_quantity: trace distance as a proper metric on density matrices

checkers.alarm: tracedist violates either side of the bound by more than 500*eps64
checkers.invariant: 1 - fidelity(A,B) <= tracedist(A,B) <= sqrt(1 - fidelity(A,B)^2), the standard textbook bound both functions' own docstrings cite (Nielsen & Chuang)
checkers.observation_point: at the return point of tracedist(), a cross-function re-call sanitizer independently calls fidelity() on the same pair and checks the double inequality
checkers.precondition: any two valid density matrices A, B of matching dimensions, any purity, any relative distinguishability Arguments of Qobj type 'super' (e.g. the Choi matrices qutip's process_fidelity passes to fidelity) are outside the precondition and are not checked (revised 2026-10-09).
checkers.rationale: this is the strongest cross-check in the module: it tests whether two independently implemented, separately documented quantities remain consistent with a well-known theorem relating them, catching joint-but-not-individually-visible defects
checkers.scientific_quantity: Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities relating fidelity and trace distance

checkers.alarm: abs(bures_dist(A,B) - bures_dist(conjugated)) exceeds 2000*eps64, or (fidelity away from 1) abs(bures_angle difference) exceeds 2000*eps64 (each plus the fidelity conditioning term amplified by 1/max(distance or sin(angle), sqrt(term)), see tolerance_derivation)
checkers.invariant: bures_dist(A,B) == bures_dist(UAU^dag, UBU^dag) and bures_angle(A,B) == bures_angle(UAU^dag, UBU^dag), since fidelity is unitarily invariant
checkers.observation_point: inside bures_dist(), a re-call sanitizer constructs a random-unitary-conjugated pair and compares
checkers.precondition: any two valid density matrices A, B of matching dimensions, compared against a unitarily-conjugated pair (U A U^dag, U B U^dag) for random unitary U, restricted to fidelity away from 1 (within 1e-6) for the bures_angle check since arccos has an unbounded derivative there Arguments of Qobj type 'super' (e.g. the Choi matrices qutip's process_fidelity passes to fidelity) are outside the precondition and are not checked (revised 2026-10-09).
checkers.rationale: both functions' entire numerical content is 'call fidelity, apply a closed-form scalar function'; a violation would isolate a bug in the type-dispatch/dimension-matching logic surrounding the fidelity call, not the trivial scalar formula itself
checkers.scientific_quantity: Bures distance and Bures angle as pure functions of fidelity alone

checkers.alarm: max over the 3 cyclic pairs of (commutator - i*third_operator).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*max(1,Jz.norm('max'))*max(1,j)
checkers.invariant: [Jx,Jy]=i*Jz and its two cyclic permutations, where Jx/Jy/Jz are each built via independent code paths from _jplus/_jz
checkers.observation_point: inside jmat(j, None), immediately before returning the (Jx,Jy,Jz) tuple
checkers.precondition: any valid non-negative integer/half-integer spin quantum number j (int(2*j)==2*j and j>=0), any data layer, evaluated at jmat(j, None)'s tuple return
checkers.rationale: Jx, Jy, Jz are built from three independently-coded expressions (not from each other), so their commutators reproducing the third operator with the correct sign/prefactor is a nontrivial cross-construction check underlying every spin-chain and angular-momentum model in QuTiP
checkers.scientific_quantity: su(2) angular-momentum commutation algebra

checkers.alarm: (comm_block - eye_block).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*(N+offset)
checkers.invariant: (destroy(N) @ create(N) - create(N) @ destroy(N)) restricted to rows/columns 0..N-2 equals the identity on that block
checkers.observation_point: inside destroy(), immediately before returning, re-calling create() with the same N/offset/dtype
checkers.precondition: any truncation size N>=2, any offset>=0, restricted to the interior block (Fock levels 0..N-2; also excluding level 0 when offset>0); the truncation boundaries are explicitly excluded as the well-known finite-truncation edge effect, not a defect
checkers.rationale: create()/destroy() are built via two independent qdiags calls placing sqrt-scaled diagonals (not create=destroy().dag()), so interior CCR agreement is a genuine cross-check that the two independently-coded diagonal placements are consistent
checkers.scientific_quantity: bosonic canonical commutation relation [a, a^dagger] = I

checkers.alarm: (U @ U.dag() - qeye(N2)).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*N2
checkers.invariant: qft(dimensions) @ qft(dimensions).dag() == qeye(N2)
checkers.observation_point: inside qft(), before returning, re-computing U @ U.dag()
checkers.precondition: any composite or scalar dimension specification producing total Hilbert space size N2>=1, any data layer
checkers.rationale: qft builds a dense matrix directly from a closed-form np.exp formula and 1/sqrt(N2) normalization; unitarity is a consequence of the DFT orthogonality theorem applied to this exact closed form, not locally checkable by inspecting the exp/meshgrid construction line by line -- a sign or normalization-exponent transcription error would still 'look like' a Fourier matrix without being unitary
checkers.scientific_quantity: discrete quantum Fourier transform unitarity

checkers.alarm: not lhs.isequal(rhs) i.e. (lhs-rhs).norm('max') > 0.0 -- exact equality, no floating-point arithmetic on nonzero entries beyond 1.0
checkers.invariant: swap(N,M) @ tensor(basis(N,n), basis(M,m)) == tensor(basis(M,m), basis(N,n)) for every valid n,m
checkers.observation_point: inside swap(), before returning, swept over a basis sample (not one hard-coded pair)
checkers.precondition: any N,M>=1, any pair of basis kets basis(N,n), basis(M,m) for valid indices n<N, m<M
checkers.rationale: swap is built from an explicit CSR row/column index formula entirely disjoint from tensor()'s own Kronecker-product construction; the docstring's claimed action is a cross-component consistency law, not a tautology of the CSR construction line, since an off-by-one or transposition error would still produce a valid permutation matrix without satisfying this specific action law
checkers.scientific_quantity: tensor-factor exchange operator's defining action on product basis states

checkers.alarm: (U.dag() @ U - qeye(N)).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*N*max(1,|m|,g) with g=|m|*sqrt((offset+N)/N) (displace) or |m|*(offset+N)/N (squeeze), plus 2*sqrt(N)*t+N*t^2 where t is the requested sparse cleanup threshold auto_tidyup_atol when auto_tidyup is on (0 otherwise)
checkers.invariant: U.dag() @ U == qeye(N) for U = displace(N, alpha) or U = squeeze(N, z), since the exponential of any anti-Hermitian generator is exactly unitary in exact arithmetic
checkers.observation_point: inside displace() and squeeze(), before returning
checkers.precondition: any truncation N>=1, any complex alpha/z with |alpha| or |z| in the swept range [0.1, 15] (larger magnitudes not covered by this sweep)
checkers.rationale: expm on a truncated matrix is computed by a general-purpose Pade/scaling-and-squaring algorithm with no a priori guarantee of returning an exactly unitary matrix at finite working precision even when the mathematical generator is exactly anti-Hermitian -- this is a genuine numerical question about expm's backward stability, not visible from the one-line .expm(dtype=dtype) call
checkers.scientific_quantity: unitarity of the matrix exponential of an anti-Hermitian generator

checkers.alarm: not result.isequal(original, tol) or result._dims != original._dims, tol=50*eps64*max(1,original.norm('max'))
checkers.invariant: operator_to_vector(vector_to_operator(v)) == v, both numerically and in dims metadata
checkers.observation_point: inside vector_to_operator(), before returning, re-calling operator_to_vector() on the freshly computed result and comparing to the original operator-ket input
checkers.precondition: any square operator-type or operator-ket-type Qobj, any data layer, any dimension
checkers.rationale: operator_to_vector and vector_to_operator each independently reconstruct SuperSpace/dims bookkeeping around the data-level reshape (via _map_over_compound_operators and separate dims derivations); a dims-metadata bug in either direction could silently produce an operator with the right shape but wrong dims labeling, which only checking both numerical content and dims agreement would catch
checkers.scientific_quantity: column-stacking vectorization bijection between operator space and its doubled vector representation

checkers.alarm: (spre(A)@spost(B) - spost(B)@spre(A)).norm('max') exceeds 100*eps64*dim^2
checkers.invariant: spre(A) @ spost(B) == spost(B) @ spre(A)
checkers.observation_point: inside spre(A), re-calling spost(A) on the same operand (B=A, a valid non-degenerate member of the precondition family)
checkers.precondition: any two square operator-type Qobjs A, B of the same Hilbert-space dimension, any data layer (CSR inputs in canonical format, no duplicate entries); A and B need not commute, be Hermitian, or be unitary
checkers.rationale: spre is built via _data.kron and spost via _data.kron_transpose, two different Kronecker-product helpers; nothing in either individual construction locally guarantees that the cross product of a kron-built matrix and a kron_transpose-built matrix commutes, even though the underlying mathematical fact (independent tensor factors after vectorization) is true
checkers.scientific_quantity: commutation of left- and right-multiplication superoperators in Liouville space

checkers.alarm: exact inequality: (reshuffle(result) - q_oper).norm('max') > 0.0
checkers.invariant: reshuffle(reshuffle(A)) == A for A in the Compound branch
checkers.observation_point: inside reshuffle(), before returning, gated on the input actually being Compound-structured, re-calling reshuffle() on the freshly computed result
checkers.precondition: any super-type or operator-ket-type Qobj built as a tensor product of k>=2 square-operator subspaces, restricted to the genuine Compound-structured branch (excluding the SuperSpace/non-compound early-return shortcuts, which are local tautologies that literally return a copy)
checkers.rationale: _to_super_of_tensor and _to_tensor_of_super independently compute a perm_idxs permutation via two separately written (non-textually-identical) loops and hand off to Qobj.permute; their composing to the identity is a nontrivial cross-function law, and reshuffle composes with permute -- a pure relabeling operation with no floating-point arithmetic on nonzero data
checkers.scientific_quantity: column-reshuffling relabeling between composite-superoperator and tensor-of-superoperator representations

checkers.alarm: (U @ U.dag() - qeye(N)).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*N + 2*sqrt(N)*t + N*t^2, with t = sqrt(2)*atol_tidy (0 when auto_tidyup is off)
checkers.invariant: U @ U.dag() == qeye(N) for U = rand_unitary(...)
checkers.observation_point: inside rand_unitary(), before returning (both distribution branches, swept across density<1 to exercise the block/shuffle path)
checkers.precondition: any dimension specification, any density in [0,1], either distribution (haar or exp), any seed
checkers.rationale: the Haar path relies on a QR decomposition followed by a sign-correction rescaling of Q by a phase-only diagonal derived from R's diagonal; if that rescaling were wrong the result would still be sampled from some distribution over matrices without being unitary in general; the exp path relies on scipy.linalg.expm of a random Hermitian generator, a distinct numerical question; density<1 additionally exercises the block-assembly/shuffle step
checkers.scientific_quantity: unitarity of a randomly sampled unitary operator

checkers.alarm: abs(rho.tr()-1) > 50*eps64*N + sqrt(2)*N*atol_tidy or min(rho.eigenenergies()) < -(50*eps64 + sqrt(2)*N*atol_tidy)
checkers.invariant: rho.tr() == 1 and min(rho.eigenenergies()) >= 0 for rho = rand_dm(...); Hermiticity is excluded from this alarm as a locally-guaranteed constructor flag
checkers.observation_point: inside rand_dm(), before returning, across all five distribution branches
checkers.precondition: any valid dimension, any of the 5 distribution choices (ginibre/hs/pure/eigen/herm) with their required parameters satisfied (e.g. eigenvalues summing to 1 within the function's own documented 1e-15*N tolerance for eigen), any seed
checkers.rationale: the ginibre/hs paths construct rho as a Gram matrix (PSD by construction, locally guaranteed), but the eigen path builds rho via repeated Jacobi rotations of a diagonal matrix of user-supplied eigenvalues, and the herm path builds it from a block-random-Hermitian matrix transformed and merged; PSD-ness of the final, trace-normalized, merged matrix is not equally locally obvious across all five branches, which is exactly why this is checked as one law over the whole family
checkers.scientific_quantity: trace and positive-semidefiniteness of a randomly sampled density matrix

checkers.alarm: (sum_K_dag_K - qeye(N)).norm('max') exceeds 50*eps64*N^2 + len(K)*(2*sqrt(2)*N+1)*atol_tidy
checkers.invariant: sum_i K_i^dagger K_i == I for the Kraus operators returned by rand_kraus_map(N)
checkers.observation_point: inside rand_kraus_map(), before returning, summing K.dag()@K over the returned list
checkers.precondition: any valid dimension N>=1, any seed
checkers.rationale: the construction takes the first N columns of a random N^3xN^3 unitary and reshapes the resulting N^3xN block into N^2 separate NxN matrices; the completeness relation is a consequence of those N columns being orthonormal combined with the specific reshape indexing being consistent with the Stinespring dilation's mathematical derivation -- a reshape bug (wrong axis order or stride) would produce N^2 matrices of the right shape from the right orthonormal columns without necessarily satisfying completeness
checkers.scientific_quantity: Kraus completeness relation defining a trace-preserving quantum channel

checkers.alarm: max(abs(axis_sums - 1)) exceeds 50*eps64*N + N*atol_tidy (atol_tidy = 0 when auto_tidyup is off)
checkers.invariant: every row of rand_stochastic(N,density,kind='right').full() sums to 1, or every column sums to 1 for kind='left', matching the function's own documented kind semantics
checkers.observation_point: inside rand_stochastic(), before returning, checking sums along the axis implied by the labeled kind, not the axis the internal division happened to normalize
checkers.precondition: any dimension N>=1, any density in the function's valid range, either kind (left or right), any seed
checkers.rationale: the construction explicitly divides each row of the pre-transpose matrix by its own row sum, then conditionally transposes for kind=='left'; checking against the labeled convention (not the raw division line) catches a bug in the transpose condition that would produce a matrix whose columns, not rows, sum to 1 while being returned under the opposite kind label
checkers.scientific_quantity: normalization of a stochastic matrix along its documented convention axis

checkers.alarm: (Tr_out(D) - qeye(N)).norm('max') exceeds 200*eps64*N^2*max(1,cond(Y)/100), where Tr_out uses np.einsum('ijik->jk', D.full().reshape(N,N,N,N)) -- the same contraction pattern the production code itself uses to compute Y
checkers.invariant: the partial trace over the output space of the intermediate (pre-permute) Choi-form matrix D equals the identity on the input space
checkers.observation_point: inside rand_super_bcsz()'s enforce_tp branch, immediately after constructing D and before the final D.permute([[1],[0]]) row/column-stacking-convention conversion
checkers.precondition: any dimension N>=1, any rank in [1,N^2], enforce_tp=True (enforce_tp=False is documented to produce only a CP, not TP, map and is explicitly excluded), any seed
checkers.rationale: the enforce_tp branch's Y^(-1/2) renormalization (via scipy.linalg.sqrtm of a matrix inverse) is a nontrivial numerical procedure whose correctness in producing a trace-preserving map is exactly what the BCSZ08 algorithm claims; a bug in the einsum partial-trace indices used to compute Y would silently produce a Y that does not correspond to the intended partial trace
checkers.scientific_quantity: trace preservation of a Choi matrix sampled from the BCSZ ensemble under enforce_tp=True

checkers.alarm: max abs entry of (dense_result - sparse_result) exceeds 50*eps64*dim + sqrt(2)*atol_tidy (atol_tidy = 0 when auto_tidyup is off)
checkers.invariant: _partial_transpose_dense(rho,mask) == _partial_transpose_sparse(rho,mask) for the same rho, mask
checkers.observation_point: inside the public partial_transpose() dispatcher, invoking both method='dense' and method='sparse' on the same input and comparing
checkers.precondition: any density-matrix-shaped Qobj with pure (non-ENR) dims, any composite structure (k>=1 subsystems), any valid boolean/0-1 mask of length k
checkers.rationale: the dense path reshapes and transposes a full ndarray using an index-permutation array, the sparse path walks CSR row pointers and uses state_index_number/state_number_index round trips per nonzero entry -- two disjoint index-bookkeeping schemes over the same composite-space labeling that must agree only because they compute the same mathematical object, not because either implementation calls the other
checkers.scientific_quantity: cross-method consistency of the partial transpose linear map

checkers.alarm: abs(result.tr() - rho.tr()) exceeds 50*eps64*dim + sqrt(2)*dim*atol_tidy (atol_tidy = 0 when auto_tidyup is off)
checkers.invariant: Tr(rho^{T_A}) == Tr(rho) for any subsystem mask A
checkers.observation_point: inside partial_transpose(), at the public dispatch level, after either implementation returns
checkers.precondition: any density-matrix-shaped Qobj with pure dims, any composite structure, any valid mask; CSR inputs in canonical format (no duplicate entries)
checkers.rationale: independent of QT-PT-001 (which checks method agreement, not correctness against the original): both implementations could agree with each other while both being wrong relative to the true partial-transpose operation; trace preservation is a genuine, independent scientific check grounded in the mathematical definition of transpose (transposing a block does not change which diagonal entries exist, only which off-diagonal entries pair with which)
checkers.scientific_quantity: trace invariance of the partial transpose

checkers.alarm: concurrence_value exceeds 1 + 50*eps64
checkers.invariant: concurrence(rho) <= 1 (the lower bound 0 is already enforced in code via np.maximum(0, lsum), a local clamp excluded from this alarm)
checkers.observation_point: inside concurrence(), before returning
checkers.precondition: any valid two-qubit density matrix (or ket/bra with [2,2] dims, auto-promoted via ket2dm), Hermitian, positive-semidefinite, unit-trace
checkers.rationale: the upper bound is not locally enforced anywhere in the function; it is a nontrivial consequence of the eigenvalue ordering and subtraction formula sqrt_evals[3]-sqrt_evals[2]-sqrt_evals[1]-sqrt_evals[0] applied to the rho_tilde=(rho@sysy)@(rho.conj()@sysy) construction -- concurrence above 1 would directly contradict the measure's definition as a normalized entanglement quantifier
checkers.scientific_quantity: Wootters concurrence entanglement measure upper bound

checkers.alarm: result < -tol, or result > 2*min(entropy_vn(ptrace(rho,selA)), entropy_vn(ptrace(rho,selB))) + tol, with tol = 200*eps64*hilbert_dim, plus, when auto_tidyup is on, F_A + F_B + 2*max(F_A, F_B) where F_X is the Fannes-Audenaert entropy-change bound for marginal X under an entrywise perturbation of at most sqrt(2)*atol_tidy
checkers.invariant: entropy_mutual(rho,selA,selB) >= 0 (subadditivity of von Neumann entropy) and <= 2*min(S(A),S(B))
checkers.observation_point: at entropy_mutual()'s return, independently re-calling entropy_vn() on the two marginals for the upper bound
checkers.precondition: any density matrix with pure dims and at least two subsystems, any partition selA/selB covering all subsystems exactly once between them, any purity/mixedness
checkers.rationale: S(A), S(B), and S(AB) are each computed via independent eigenenergies() calls with their own numerical error, and subadditivity is a deep theorem about von Neumann entropy, not an algebraic identity of the three-term subtraction; a sign error or off-by-one in which reduced state is subtracted from which would still produce some number from the formula without satisfying either bound in general
checkers.scientific_quantity: quantum mutual information subadditivity and boundedness

checkers.alarm: abs(rho_ss.tr()-1) exceeds 200*eps64*max(1,(n/4)**2), or min(rho_ss.eigenenergies()) < -200*eps64*max(1,(n/4)**2), n the Hilbert dimension of rho_ss
checkers.invariant: rho_ss.tr() == 1 and min(rho_ss.eigenenergies()) >= 0
checkers.observation_point: inside steadystate(), immediately before returning rho_ss, for all 4 linear-algebra solver branches (including the eigen and svd branches that return early)
checkers.precondition: any super-type Liouvillian A (or Hamiltonian+collapse-operator list from which one is built internally), method in {direct, eigen, svd, power}, and the Liouvillian has a unique stationary state (numerical nullity 1: second-smallest singular value of L above n*eps64*sigma_max, n the Hilbert dimension); with a degenerate stationary manifold any null vector is a valid steady state and the check is skipped. Methods 'propagator' and 'iterative' are excluded: their accuracy is set by the caller's own stopping criterion.
checkers.rationale: a solver could return a vector that is a null vector of L but not a valid density matrix (wrong trace normalization or a sign-indefinite combination of null vectors); unit trace and positive semidefiniteness are physical requirements independent of the solver's internal convergence criterion
checkers.scientific_quantity: physical validity (unit-trace, PSD) of a returned steady state

checkers.alarm: (recovered - scale*oper).norm('max') exceeds 100*eps64*prod(dims)*max(1,max|scale*oper|) + sqrt(2)*(scale+2)*atol_tidy (atol_tidy = 0 when auto_tidyup is off)
checkers.invariant: expand_operator(oper, dims, targets).ptrace(targets) == prod(dims[i] for i not in targets) * oper
checkers.observation_point: inside expand_operator(), before returning, re-calling .ptrace(targets) on the freshly constructed result
checkers.precondition: any operator oper acting on a subset of subsystems matching the dimensions at the chosen targets positions within dims, any valid dims list of length N>=2, any subset targets of {0,...,N-1} given in ascending order (single or multiple, contiguous or non-contiguous), any data layer
checkers.rationale: expand_operator builds a new_order permutation from an identity-list-plus-tensor-plus-permute construction distinct from a plain two-operand tensor() call (which QT-QOBJ-004 already covers); this exercises expand_operator's own new_order bookkeeping arithmetic specifically -- a bug there could exist even if both tensor() and permute() individually satisfy their own sanitizers
checkers.scientific_quantity: recovery of an embedded operator via partial trace over its complementary subsystems
